state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s presented with a 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis. He was initially treated with oral steroids. At presentation, he denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits. He had no other significant medical history.

Patient had complete right facial paralysis and a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal. Audiographic findings showed mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz, but were otherwise normal.

{'Imaging Studies': {'MRI': '- MRI scan showed a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen that had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast.\n- Follow-up MRI (9 months post-op) showed heterogeneous signal in the stylomastoid foramen on T2 images', 'CT': 'Imaging showed expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve, erosion of the posterior external auditory canal, and expansion of the stylomastoid foramen'}, 'Pathology': {'Gross Examination': '2 × 1.5 × 0.5-cm tan to brown, rubbery specimen consisted of cartilage', 'Microscopic Examination': 'Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67. Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index', 'Image Description': 'Microscopic image showing increased numbers of atypical pleomorphic nuclei in a myxochondroid matrix. Hyperchromasia and binucleate forms were found although mitoses were not'}}

Options:

C. Low-grade chondrosarcoma of the mastoid with facial nerve involvement
D. Benign chondroma
